A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 30-page versions of the same research work. Their main sections, algorithms, figures, table, and Appendices A–H can be reliably matched despite renaming and pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original MNIST, SST-2, HAR, and CIFAR-100 experiments, Gaussian simulations including 1,000-trial results, and experiments using certified calibration samples.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised experimental outcomes in Section 6, the appendix figures, and Table 1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces previously stored scores κ_j with scores κ_rj recomputed through added inner loops before ranking against κ_rr. This changes the documented computation for data-dependent scores, while retaining the score models, KS statistics, p-value combination, and confidence-set construction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian, MNIST, SST-2, HAR, and CIFAR-100 tasks. Mixed-sentiment changes, no-changepoint simulations, and scenarios with certified pre-change or post-change samples are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the oracle, parametric learned, and KDE learned score comparisons at both confidence levels. The alternative testing and discrepancy methods discussed as evaluated elsewhere also remain unchanged; no new external baseline is evaluated.

E3.justification: Reported sample sizes, changepoints, classifiers, KDE bandwidth rules, confidence levels, and testing procedures are retained. Figure 9's new legend says 400, but its marker, caption, and experimental description still indicate 300; this is a labeling inconsistency rather than an established setting change.

E4.justification: Appendix A revises the evidence comparing learned scores with oracle scores, including their relative localization errors in Table 1 and the curves in Figure 10. The analysis questions and comparator choices remain unchanged, with no new robustness or sensitivity investigation.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 trials for the Gaussian comparison and 1,000 simulations for each pretesting condition, using the same coverage uncertainty reporting. No new seed information, uncertainty procedure, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical outcomes change across all four main experimental examples and several Table 1 entries. MNIST's confidence set changes from [371,432] to [374,423], HAR's size-24 set becomes [376,444], and CIFAR-100's set changes from [268,329] to [263,316]. SST-2 sets and estimates also change. In Table 1, KDE's 95% row changes mean absolute deviation from 35.15 to 15.29, while oracle entries remain unchanged. These are substantial revisions to reported evidence, not uniformly improved performance.

T1.justification: The coverage proof is revised around κ_rj scores and explicitly cites Vovk et al. (2003), Proposition 3.1, for independence. Section 5 reverses the rank comparisons in p_n[s] and T_n[s] from '<' to '>', and Appendix E removes the mixture decomposition in the Neyman–Pearson proof. These are mathematical revisions to existing results; the retained optimality inequality is inconsistent with the reversed T_n definition.

C1.justification: The claims of finite-sample coverage under exchangeability, useful learned scores, and broad empirical applicability remain. v4 highlights the conformal Neyman–Pearson lemma in its abstract, but this contribution was already stated in v3's introduction and Theorem 5.1.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning learned-score effectiveness, certified-sample benefits, subtle changes, and pretesting remain. The single-changepoint scope, exchangeability requirements, and absence of theoretical guarantees for the point estimator are also retained.

D1.justification: Section 6 changes the reported runtime from under three minutes to under ten seconds per experiment on the same M1 Pro CPU. The code-access information, CNN architecture and training details, classifier identities, and KDE specifications remain unchanged; the runtime revision is not explained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work positioning remain unchanged. Appendix E adds a precise proposition reference to the already-cited Vovk et al. (2003), without changing the paper's novelty positioning or introducing another cited work.

P1.justification: The title changes, CONCH is renamed MCP throughout, and the abstract highlights an existing theoretical contribution. Section 3's explanatory paragraphs are locally rewritten and reordered, while the overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Several experimental plots are redrawn with changed axis scales, Algorithm 1 expands, and figures move relative to surrounding text, including Figure 9 moving after the conclusion. Figure 9 introduces the inconsistent changepoint legend. The same twelve figures and Table 1 retain their overall display structure.

improvement.justification: v4's rescoring revision better aligns the left-side algorithm with the exchangeability argument, and the proof attribution becomes more precise. However, its new right-side loop leaves κ_rr undefined despite using it subsequently, and reversing T_n's comparison leaves the retained optimality and rejection inequalities inconsistent. These competing corrections and defects prevent a reliable net-quality judgment; the updated empirical values alone do not establish improvement.
